body.statement:
Under ass:density-positivity, ass:density-smoothness, ass:inner-ellipticity, ass:outer-ellipticity, ass:lift-regularity, ass:fixed-separated-grid, ass:kernel-symmetry, ass:kernel-mass, ass:kernel-order, ass:four-sample-design, and ass:polynomial-bandwidth, the following estimates hold uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\).  For \(h=h_n\), every coordinate of the score \(\Psi_{g,h}\) is the sum of its frozen-coefficient, first-order-coordinate Green score and a remainder whose \(L^2(P_g)\) norm is bounded by a common constant.  In particular,
\[
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G}\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}
 \leq C\sqrt{L_n},
 \qquad
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G}\mathbb E_{P_g}\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}(X)\rVert^4
 \leq C h_n^{-2}.
\]
For the opposite-fold adjoint scores,
\[
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G,\ r\in\{1,2\}}
 L_n^{-1/2}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\]
and, on events whose probabilities tend to one uniformly,
\[
 \max_{g,r}\mathbb E_{P_g}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}(X)\rVert^4
 \leq C h_n^{-2}.
\]
Moreover, if \(u=(u_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) is a zero-integral four-density perturbation, the perturbed densities are positive, and \(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{2,1/4}}\) is smaller than a common constant, then the selected lifted nested map in def:identified-functional obeys
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}
 \left\lVert
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j
 \right\rVert
 \leq C\left(\max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,1/4}}\right)^2.
\]
For the signed periodized KDEs,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}
 \mathbb E_P\left[\max_g
 \lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{1,1/4}}^4\right]
 \leq C\left\{
 \frac{\log n}{n h_n^{9/2}}+h_n^{2s-5/2}
 \right\}^2,
\]
and there are constants \(c_0,C_0,\epsilon_0>0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\left(
 \max_g\lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{2,1/4}}>\epsilon_0
 \right)
 \leq C_0\exp(-c_0 n h_n^{13/2}).
\]
On the complementary good event clipping is inactive, normalization is exactly one, the selected lift branches are the population branches, all population and pilot coefficients are uniformly elliptic, and every pilot pole differs from its population pole by \(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\).
body.justification: The energy residual and weighted-Hodge harmonic block are now controlled separately.
body.gap: Transformed kernels, estimated poles, fourth moments, opposite-fold stability, and the mixed two-endpoint remainder remain unresolved.
body.consumer: This remains the analytic gate for covariance, Gaussian, ellipse, and upper-risk claims.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\vartheta=1/4\), and, for \(k=0,1,2\), put
\[
 q_{k,n}=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{,2+2k+2\vartheta}}}
          +h_n^{,s-k-\vartheta}.
\tag{1}
\]
These are exactly the three displayed rates in the statement.  We first establish the pilot bounds.  Differentiating the periodized kernel \(k\) times, applying the exponential-moment inequality
\(e^x\leq1+x+x^2e^{|x|}/2\) to each bounded centered summand, and taking a union bound on a torus lattice of mesh \(h_n n^{-3}\), gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P\!\left(
 \lVert\widetilde f_g-E_P\widetilde f_g\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}}>z
 \right)
 \leq Cn^C\exp\{-c n h_n^{2+2k+2\vartheta}z^2\}
\tag{2}
\]
for \(0<z\leq1\), uniformly in \(P\) and \(g\).  To pass from the lattice to the torus, apply the mean-value theorem to the differentiated kernel on every lattice square; the deterministic oscillation is absorbed by the same bound with derivative order \(k+1\).  Integration of (2) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\lVert\widetilde f_g-E_P\widetilde f_g\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}}^4
 \leq C\left\{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{2+2k+2\vartheta}}\right\}^{2}.
\tag{3}
\]
Taylor expansion of \(f_g(x-hu)\) through order \(s-1\), followed by ass:kernel-order and ass:kernel-mass, gives
\[
 \lVert E_P\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}}
 \leq Ch_n^{s-k-\vartheta}.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4) prove the asserted fourth-moment bound when \(k=1\).  With \(k=2\), a fixed threshold in (2), and absorption of the polynomial prefactor, they also give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\!\left(
 \max_g\lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}>\epsilon_0
 \right)\leq C_0e^{-c_0nh_n^{13/2}}.
\tag{5}
\]
By lem:mixed-bandwidth-feasibility and ass:polynomial-bandwidth,
\[
 q_{2,n}=o(1),\qquad q_{0,n}/h_n=o(1),qquad
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\,q_{1,n}q_{0,n}=o(1).
\tag{6}
\]

We next prove the critical Green estimate, including the torus localization.  Fix a pole \(y\) and write \(B_y=B(y)\).  In a coordinate ball of radius less than \(\delta_0/8\), let
\[
 \Gamma_y(z)=-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B_y}}
 \log|B_y^{-1/2}(z-y)|.
\tag{7}
\]
Choose a smooth cutoff \(\chi\) supported in the ball and equal to one near \(y\).  Before testing any singular expression, define
\[
 F_y(z)=\{B(z)-B_y\}\chi(z)\nabla\Gamma_y(z)
\tag{8}
\]
and construct \(w_y\in H^1_0\) as the minimizer of the coercive energy with weak forcing \(\operatorname{div}F_y\) plus the bounded cutoff terms.  This construction is legitimate because uniform \(C^{0,\vartheta}\) control of \(B\) gives
\[
 |F_y(z)|\leq C|z-y|^{-1+\vartheta},
 \qquad F_y\in L^2.
\tag{9}
\]
Only after this construction do we test the weak equation and obtain \(\lVert\nabla w_y\rVert_2\leq C\).  The difference between the periodic Green function and the resulting local Dirichlet Green function is \(B\)-harmonic in a smaller ball.  Its gradient is uniformly bounded there by the interior estimate in lem:elliptic-green-gradient-bound, while compactness and the normalized energy estimate bound it away from the pole.  Rescaling (8) on dyadic annuli and applying the same interior estimate yields the more precise expansion
\[
 \nabla_zG_B(y,z)=\nabla\Gamma_y(z)+R_y(z),
 \qquad |R_y(z)|\leq C|z-y|^{-1+\vartheta},
 \qquad \sup_y\lVert R_y\rVert_2\leq C.
\tag{10}
\]
This proves the required periodic statement rather than importing a boundary-domain estimate across the torus seam.

Apply Fubini before estimating a KDE response.  Every leading cell-
\(g\) influence at point \(y_j\) can then be written
\[
 \psi^0_{g,j,h}(x)=K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0_{g,j}(x)
 -P_g(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0_{g,j}),
\tag{11}
\]
where \(\zeta^0_{g,j}\) is the frozen expression (7), pulled back to the original cell coordinate by either \(R_0\) or \(T\), and multiplied by the corresponding coefficient \(1\) or \(\alpha(y_j)\).  The exact change of variables cancels the Jacobian in the transformed kernel tangent.  Thus no approximation of a nonlinear kernel argument has been made in (11).  Taylor's formula for the smooth pullback \(\Phi\), uniformly for \(|v|\leq Ch\), is
\[
 \Phi(x+v)-\Phi(x)-D\Phi(x)v
 =\int_0^1(1-t)D^2\Phi(x+tv)[v,v],dt,
 \qquad |\cdot|\leq Ch^2.
\tag{12}
\]
Together with (10), (12) shows that the difference between the exact first-order-coordinate Green influence and \(\zeta^0_{g,j}\) has uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\) norm.  The second, order-minus-two term in def:nested-derivative has kernel bounded by
\[
 C\int_{\mathbb T^2}\frac{dz}{d(z,y_j)d(z,x)}
 \leq C\{1+|\log d(x,y_j)|\},
\tag{13}
\]
and hence also belongs uniformly to \(L^2\).  The weighted-Hodge construction in thm:nested-derivative gives the same bound for every harmonic term.  Young's inequality applied only after these \(L^2\) bounds have been established proves
\[
 \lVert\Psi_{g,h}-\psi^0_{g,h}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}\leq C,
 \qquad \lVert\Psi_{g,h}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}\leq C\sqrt{\log(1/h)}.
\tag{14}
\]

For clarity, the mollification calculation behind (14) is explicit.  A frozen singular field \(z^0(x)\) satisfies \(|z^0(x)|\leq C/d(x,x_0)\).  On \(d(x,x_0)>Ch\), kernel symmetry and (12) imply
\[
 |K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*z^0(x)-z^0(x)|\leq Ch,d(x,x_0)^{-2},
\tag{15}
\]
whereas on \(d(x,x_0)\leq Ch\) both sides are bounded by \(C/h\).  Radial integration gives
\[
 \int_{d\leq Ch}|K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*z^0|^2=O(1),
 \qquad
 \int_{d>Ch}|K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*z^0-z^0|^2=O(1).
\tag{16}
\]
The same split, with fourth powers, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_g}\lVert\Psi_{g,h}(X)\rVert^4\leq Ch^{-2}.
\tag{17}
\]
The centering terms are bounded because \(1/d(\cdot,x_0)\) is integrable in dimension two.  Equations (10)--(17) prove the first two score assertions in the lemma, including all generated-target and harmonic pieces.

We now treat estimated coefficients and moving poles.  On the event in (5), the two augmented systems of thm:nested-derivative and their adjoints have common ellipticity and Schur-complement constants.  Their deterministic stability estimates and (1)--(4) imply
\[
 \epsilon_n^{\rm coef}:=max_{g,r}
 \{\lVert\widehat B^{(-r)}-B\rVert_{C^1}
   +\lVert\widehat{\mathsf C}^{(-r)}-\mathsf C\rVert_{C^1}
   +\lVert\widehat\alpha^{(-r)}-\alpha\rVert_{C^1}\}=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\tag{18}
\]
and every estimated pole obeys
\[
 d_n^{\rm pole}\leq Cq_{0,n}=o_{\mathbb P}(h_n).
\tag{19}
\]
For a mollified \(1/d\) field, differentiation with respect to its pole and (16) give
\[
 \lVert K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*z^0(\cdot-d)-K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*z^0\rVert_2
 \leq C|d|/h.
\tag{20}
\]
The resolvent identity for each scalar or adjoint inverse,
\[
 \mathcal L_{\widehat B}^{-1}-\mathcal L_B^{-1}
 =\mathcal L_{\widehat B}^{-1}
   (\mathcal L_B-\mathcal L_{\widehat B})\mathcal L_B^{-1},
\tag{21}
\]
and the analogous finite-dimensional Schur-complement identity show that coefficient perturbations contribute at most
\(C\epsilon_n^{\rm coef}\sqrt{L_n}\) in \(L^2\).  The order-minus-two and harmonic parts contribute \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n})\) by their bounded \(L^2\) envelopes.  From (18)--(21),
\[
 \max_{g,r}L_n^{-1/2}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{22}
\]
The pointwise version of the same annular split is bounded by \(C/(d+h_n)\); raising it to the fourth power and integrating proves, on the good event,
\[
 \max_{g,r}\mathbb E_{P_g}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}(X)\rVert^4\leq Ch_n^{-2}.
\tag{23}
\]

It remains to prove the nonlinear assertion.  Equations (31)--(33) in the proof of thm:nested-derivative apply uniformly on the event
\(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}<\epsilon_0\).  They give the stronger two-endpoint estimate
\[
 \max_j\left\lVert
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j\right\rVert
 \leq C\left(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}\right)
          \left(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}\right).
\tag{24}
\]
Since the \(C^{0,\vartheta}\) norm is bounded by the \(C^{1,\vartheta}\) norm, (24) implies the displayed quadratic inequality in the lemma.  Combining (3)--(6) and (24) proves that its stochastic value is
\(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n/n})\).  The kernel moment expansion gives the deterministic transport bias \(O(h_n^{s-2})\), and lem:mixed-bandwidth-feasibility makes its normalized value vanish.

Finally, on the event in (5), \(\lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_\infty<c/2\), so clipping is inactive.  Ass:kernel-mass and periodization give \(\int\widetilde f_g=1\), hence the normalizer is exactly one.  Stability of the augmented systems plus ass:lift-regularity keeps both maps on their population branches, preserves ellipticity, and, by (19), places every pilot pole within \(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\) of its population pole.  This proves all assertions of the lemma.
